chain_lifetime: __schedule clears the selected root donor link immediately before find_proxy_task while rq lock is held. Each further owner link is assigned only after on_rq/CPU/migration checks verify a queued owner on that same rq; the link points back into the chain just walked, not an arbitrary previous scheduling chain.

proxy_migrate_task has one call site, the remote-owner branch of that walk. Current-in-chain returns resched-idle before migration. Goto exits the primitive/task lock guards but keeps rq lock. The reverse chain terminates at the cleared root and is read under the uninterrupted source rq lock.

deactivate_task writes TASK_ON_RQ_MIGRATING before dequeue (not on_rq=0). Native __task_rq_lock spins/retries while that state is set, serializing remote ttwu. The chain is converted to a local se.group_node list before source rq unlock. Target attach holds target rq lock and sets queued only through activate_task. Thus the direct migration traversal has a source-state lifetime argument distinct from saved unlock hints.

Current task unlock paths may retain links after remote wakeup/reset, so they cannot use the migration argument. bb6c4caa1ee2 uses pointer identity only until finding a live waiter under wait_lock; cancellation cannot unlink/free that waiter under the same lock. Remaining rwsem link comparisons/clears do not dereference the saved pointer.

No other direct blocked_donor consumers were found in the complete local kernel C/header scan. This bounds this source audit; it is not proof about arbitrary external modules, all schedulers, callback misconduct, lock bugs or hardware interleavings.
